title: Love people
hookLine: asked about humaneness, Confucius said: love people (Analects 12.22)
carry: he didn't ask about the horses

cards: What does it mean to be humane? A student named Fan Chi put that question to his teacher. Not a question about the stars, or the gods, or how to get ahead: just the meaning of one word.
The teacher was Confucius, and his answer, in plain English, comes to two words. The conversation is in the Analects, a book of his sayings that tradition says his followers gathered.

teach.b: The word is ren. It's been translated as benevolence, humaneness, goodness, perfect virtue.

teach.h: IT IS TO LOVE ALL MEN.
teach.b: In James Legge's old translation, Fan Chi asked about benevolence, and "The Master said, 'It is to love all men.'" Love people. Not an idea of people: people themselves, starting with the ones in front of you.
In the same passage, Fan Chi also asks about knowledge, and the answer matches: know people. The Analects keeps one small scene that shows ren better than a definition.
The stables burned while Confucius was away at court. When he came home, he asked whether anyone had been hurt.

teach.h: HE DIDN'T ASK ABOUT THE HORSES.
teach.b: The text adds that he didn't ask about the horses.
For Confucius, love grows outward through real relationships: parents, siblings, friends, neighbors, rulers and the ruled.
Another saying in the Analects describes the humane person as one who, wanting to stand firm, helps others stand firm too.
Love here isn't mainly a feeling. It's a way of treating people, practiced in a household, then a street, then a whole society: ordinary conduct, done humanely, again and again.

how: In Confucian tradition, ren (humaneness) is practiced through everyday relationships: honoring family, keeping faith with friends, and treating others with care.

o: respect for elders and good manners
humaneness: treating real people with love
loyalty owed to the ruler alone

practice: Think back over the last day for one moment when someone was treated as a means to an end, by you or toward you, a cashier, a coworker, someone on the phone, and just see it, without judging.
Then choose one person you'll meet and one small way to treat them humanely, their name, a real question, your full patience, and hold that intention for the rest of the sit.

wordCard.voice: Ren. Humaneness in the Analects, which Confucius explained to Fan Chi in plain words: love people. Today's word.

orig.note: Chinese: humaneness, benevolence, the virtue Fan Chi asks about in the Analects.
